spec.title: Glossary
spec.p: One definition per term, and the only place a term is defined. Every other page links here the first time it uses a word from this list.

adaptation.title: adaptation
adaptation.p: A version of documentation in another language: a separate package that mirrors the source block for block and is free sentence by sentence. This manual says «translation» and «adaptation» for the same thing. See *translation*.

agent-session.title: agent session
agent-session.p: One run of a coding agent in a project, from the moment it reads its instruction file to the moment it stops. The boot lane is what vibe prepares for the start of a session.

anchor.title: anchor
anchor.p: The identifier of a section or a fact inside a specification, the part after `#` in an address. Once published, an anchor never changes; a rename leaves a tombstone.

block-number.title: block number
block-number.p: The ordinal `pNN` every block of a documentation page receives at build time; the same in the web page, the Markdown and the XML, so a human and an agent cite one place. It names the current text and may shift after an edit, like a line number.

boot-lane.title: boot lane
boot-lane.p: The ordered reading list an agent follows at the start of a session: the managed block in the instruction file, then `STATIC.xml` in full, then the entries of `INDEX.md`. Computed by vibe from the dependency graph, never written by hand.

boot-snippet.title: boot snippet
boot-snippet.p: A package's contribution to the boot lane: one short text declared in `[boot_snippet]` with a category, read at every session start by every consumer. Documentation packages have none.

capability.title: capability
capability.p: An abstract ability a package provides or requires, written `namespace:name` with an optional version constraint; the resolver matches requirers with providers at install time.

community.title: community documentation
community.p: Documentation of a package that declares its subject but is not named by the subject: shown on the site with its publisher, below the official shelf. See *official documentation*.

companion.title: companion
companion.p: A package tied to another by name for the default case of officiality and by nothing else: the documentation `<name>-docs` of a package, or the translation `<docname>-<lang>` of a documentation. A companion keeps its own version line and stays outside family unison.

contribution.title: contribution
contribution.p: A binding of a handler to an extension point, declared as an `[[extension]]` table in a package or a project; the unit the lifecycle runs and reports.

coordinate.title: coordinate
coordinate.p: The name of a package: a group, a slash and a name, `org.vibevm.world/wal`, with `@version` when a version is meant. The kind is not part of it.

deploy-profile.title: deploy profile
deploy-profile.p: A named, ordered list of targets and the providers that apply packaged artifacts to them; `vibe deploy` runs one profile, `vibe undeploy` reverses it.

embedded-registry.title: embedded registry
embedded-registry.p: The in-tree packages of a source-built vibe, consulted automatically as a registry: first for a developer's build, after the declared registries for a distributed one.

extension-point.title: extension point
extension-point.p: A named place in the lifecycle a contribution binds to: a phase, a slot inside a phase, or a position in the boot compiler, written `family:name`.

fact.title: fact
fact.p: One anchored unit of a specification with a status: a rule, a decision, a lead-in. In XML an element named after its id with `fact="true"`; in Markdown a paragraph opening with `@fact:ID`. The addressable atom an agent cites.

family.title: family
family.p: A set of packages sharing a name stem that move in unison: the bundle `<family>`, the language guide `<family>-lang`, the server `<family>-mcp`. A change to any member bumps every member to one version.

feature.title: feature
feature.p: An optional, additive content set of a package, declared in `[features]` and activated at install; features may depend on features.

fingerprint.title: fingerprint
fingerprint.p: The hash of a package's shippable tree, the identity half of a package version, recorded as `content_hash` in the lock file and verified on every fetch.

freshness-fingerprint.title: freshness fingerprint
freshness-fingerprint.p: The hash of a phase run's declared inputs, recorded under `.vibe/`; a phase whose freshness fingerprint did not change is skipped on the next run.

git-source.title: git source
git-source.p: A dependency declared by a git repository and a tag, commit or branch instead of a registry; identity and fingerprint discipline are the same, and a branch is re-walked on update.

handler.title: handler
handler.p: What a contribution runs: a built-in, a script, a binary, a native library, or an agent prompt.

hook.title: hook
hook.p: A package's `pre-install` or `post-install` script, run in the package's slot; installing the package is the consent to run it, and its effects are not tracked.

index-registry.title: index (of a registry)
index-registry.p: A repository beside a registry's packages that records every published version's summary and fingerprint; a cache that speeds search and cold installs and is never the truth.

kind.title: kind
kind.p: What a package is for, one of eight: `flow`, `feat`, `stack`, `tool`, `lang`, `mcp`, `doc`, `app`. Metadata, not identity; the set grows only by amendment.

lifecycle.title: lifecycle
lifecycle.p: The fixed order of build steps vibe runs: the one-phase `clean` lifecycle and the nine-phase `default` lifecycle from `validate` to `deploy`. See *phase*.

link-type.title: link type
link-type.p: How a dependency's boot snippet enters a consumer's lane: `static`, compiled into `STATIC.xml`, or `dynamic`, listed in `INDEX.md` and read on demand; set by the consumer, suggested by the package.

lock-file.title: lock file
lock-file.p: `vibe.lock`: the recorded resolution, one per workspace, with every package's exact version, fingerprint and provenance. Written by vibe, committed by you.

managed-block.title: managed block
managed-block.p: The region between the lines `<vibevm>` and `</vibevm>` at the end of `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md`, the only part of those files vibe writes; it points an agent at the boot lane.

manifest.title: manifest
manifest.p: `vibe.toml`: the one file you write to describe a project, a package or a workspace; its tables decide the node's role.

mcp-server.title: MCP server
mcp-server.p: A program an agent talks to over the Model Context Protocol. vibe's own server exposes a project's packages; a package of kind `mcp` delivers servers of its own.

mirror.title: mirror
mirror.p: An alternative address for the same registry, tried for availability and verified against the same fingerprints; never recorded in the lock file.

official.title: official documentation
official.p: Documentation whose edges converge: the subject names the package in `[documentation]` or by the `-docs` convention, and the package names the subject in `[[documents]]`. One may be primary. Computed at every render, stored nowhere as a flag.

override.title: override
override.p: A replacement source for one coordinate that short-circuits the registries; marked in the lock file so nobody mistakes it for a published version.

package.title: package
package.p: The unit vibe installs: a folder with a manifest and the text or tools it delivers, published as its own repository, identified by its coordinate, version and content hash. A package is a project made installable.

phase.title: phase
phase.p: One step of a lifecycle: `validate`, `install`, `generate`, `build`, `test`, `create`, `verify`, `package`, `deploy`. Naming a phase runs every phase before it.

project.title: project
project.p: Any folder with a `vibe.toml`; a consumer of packages, marked by a `[project]` table, or a workspace of them.

provider.title: provider
provider.p: What answers how a mechanism runs: a built-in or a package-supplied implementation of a build, package or deploy step, or a model endpoint behind an agent handler. Selected by exact route or pin.

receipt.title: receipt
receipt.p: The record a deploy writes for every resource it created: what, where, under which generation, owned by which profile. The only authority for removal.

registry.title: registry
registry.p: A hosting organisation where packages are published, one repository per package; a project lists the registries it trusts in order.

relay.title: relay
relay.p: The mailbox under `.vibe/agentic/` where vibe parks an instruction it cannot execute itself; the agent drains it with `vibe command`.

scrape.title: scrape
scrape.p: The terminal removal of the vibe layer from a project, by contract, with a plan and a health proof; not to be confused with `clean`.

skill.title: skill
skill.p: A file a package declares in `[[skill]]` that teaches an agent something; `vibe skill install` projects it into the agents' skill folders.

specification.title: specification
specification.p: The normative text of a package or a project under `vibevm/vibespecs/`: addressable units with statuses, in Markdown or the XML dialect. What documentation quotes and never restates.

store.title: store
store.p: The machine-wide cache of fetched package versions under `~/.vibe/cache/`, keyed by identity, shared by every project, emptied only on request.

subject.title: subject
subject.p: A package that a documentation package documents, named in its `[[documents]]` table with a version range.

subskill.title: subskill
subskill.p: A selectable cut of a package's content, activated by the consumer's context, such as the library version a project uses.

traceability-map.title: traceability map
traceability-map.p: `specmap.json`: the generated graph of specification units, tagged code items and the edges between them, checked by the build and queried by `vibe explain`, `vibe query` and `vibe select`.

translation.title: translation
translation.p: A separate documentation package in another language that names its source in `[translates]` and mirrors its tree; official when published by the source's group under `<docname>-<lang>`. See *adaptation*.

version-constraint.title: version constraint
version-constraint.p: What a manifest asks for: a range such as `^1.0`, an exact `=1.2.0`, or nothing for the newest stable. The lock file records the one version the resolver chose within it.

workspace.title: workspace
workspace.p: A repository developing several packages together, declared by a `[workspace]` table listing member paths; one lock file at the root and one unified resolution across members.
